client_situation.text: The issuing body is the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), which is procuring the study on behalf of the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts.

MoDOT's Right of Way function must describe every realty right it acquires, conveys or leases by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4-1/4 calls, reciting specific rights when less than fee simple title is taken.

Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, and a professional land surveyor must review each description against the right of way plans before a deed is presented to the grantor.

The business driver is to determine whether Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning can produce a usable "first draft" legal land description from MHTC parameters that MoDOT Right of Way staff would then review and edit.
The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that Division.
MoDOT's Research Director, Jen Harper, is MHTC's designated representative for administering the agreement and may delegate authority to others.
MoDOT operates on a fiscal year running July 1 to June 30, which drives the quarterly reporting cycle submitted to FHWA.

goal.text: The client wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," that determines the usefulness of AI/ML for generating first-draft legal land descriptions.

The Offeror must deliver a proof of concept demonstrating how the chosen technology creates draft legal land descriptions across a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback.
The Offeror must name the program it will use to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c can proceed.

Deliverables include a literature review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, a Data Management Plan, training and a user manual for ROW staff, a draft and final report, a 1-2 page research summary, and a presentation to MoDOT staff.
The contract period is 15 months, with the schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due and contract ending February 2, 2026.

Key milestones are a kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024, the Data Management Plan on 12/4/2024, MoDOT-supplied example LLDs on 12/20/2024, an AI/ML demonstration on 4/25/2025, training and manual on 7/25/2025, an interim presentation on 9/15/2025, the draft final report on 11/3/2025, and the final report on 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must provide monthly e-mail and phone updates, quarterly status meetings with minutes, and quarterly written updates due by the last working day of March, June, September and December.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are due by 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024 to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, with receipt acknowledged by noon the same day.
All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 4 p.m. Central on July 17, 2024; contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions publicly on 7/31/2024 and notifies submitters of project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.
Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, with responsiveness determined first and then evaluation by the Technical Advisory Committee against criteria the RFP does not list or weight.
The proposal must include a narrative Work Plan of no more than 10 pages at 12-point font or larger, covering all Section 2 items and recognizing MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

The proposal must document experience delivering these services in the past three years, list at least three client references from the past three years, and identify any Sub-Offerors with full contact information.

The proposal must be submitted as one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal, personnel, organization experience, team member experience, and client references.
Failure to submit all data required under paragraph (B) is deemed sufficient cause for disqualification.

constraints.text: Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, and the cost estimate must be entered on the Section (4) Price Page line items for Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration, Miscellaneous and Total.

Any application must be built on .NET 6.0 or above (or .NET Framework 4.8 or above), use MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, and be written in C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML or Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team approves larger use.
No third-party tool or software that places a licensing responsibility on MoDOT may be used without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management.

Applications must be web-based, require no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets or Silverlight), run on Oracle 19C or a supported SQL Server version, and meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard.
No personally identifiable information may be stored in any database table without a specific business need and approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.
A Data Management Plan is due to MoDOT within 2 weeks after the kick-off meeting and must describe data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and all information MHTC supplies, remain MHTC property, and records must be kept available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years after final payment.

Offerors are encouraged to reach 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation while remaining fully liable for subcontractor performance, and may be asked before signing to provide insurance of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence for general and automobile liability plus Missouri workers' compensation.

The Offeror must submit the Exhibit A sworn affidavit of E-Verify enrollment and no unauthorized alien employment, and sole proprietorships or partnerships must also submit the Exhibit B affidavit of lawful presence.

The RFP refers bidders to documents it does not include: the Standard Research Agreement, the Proposal Submission Form, the Price Page template, the Publication Guidelines and research summary template, all posted at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.

chunk_summaries.summary: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission requests proposals from qualified organizations—private consultants, universities, and research organizations—for project TR202504, "Using AI /ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions." The work is to be coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division. Proposals must include a project plan, the proposed project team and its background, and any related projects now active or recently completed by the firm. Proposals are due to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. (Central). The letter is dated June 26, 2024, is signed by Jen Harper, Research Director, and references an attachment and the page https://www.modot.org/information-researchers under RFP documents.

The RFP (TR202504) seeks proposals from qualified organizations ("Offeror") to furnish the described services to the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission ("MHTC"). MHTC reserves the right to reject any and all proposals for any reason whatsoever. Time is of the essence for responding to the RFP within the submission deadlines.

The document is an RFP from qualified organizations to conduct the TR202504 study, "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions". The study is for the MHTC and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT).

Client is MHTC (with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts). Property descriptions must accurately define land areas or rights to be acquired, conveyed or leased, reciting specific rights if less than fee simple title, and be described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls. Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method unless the property is acquired in its entirety; when acquired in its entirety the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record. Descriptions prepared on behalf of MHTC must meet requirements in the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2. Before presenting a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or other such document to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel corresponds with the right of way plans and that the right of way plans correspond with survey information gathered by the professional land surveyor. The research project's goal is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to develop a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) using the MHTC parameters, which could be reviewed and edited by MoDOT's Right of Way staff.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30.
The contract period will run for 15 months. A copy of the Standard Research Agreement can be found on the website at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.

The chunk sets out MoDOT's RFP Schedule of Events for TR202504, with event times between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central; MoDOT may expand the schedule at its sole discretion without notification except for the proposal deadline date. 6/26/2024: MoDOT posts the RFP at https://www.modot.org/research-requests-proposal. Comments or questions must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov; 7/17/2024 4 p.m. (Central) is the only acceptable contact method, contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification, including all requests for information, data and manuals. 7/31/2024: MoDOT posts responses to questions/comments publicly on the same website. 8/21/2024 10 a.m. (Central): proposals must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day. 9/18/2024: MoDOT notifies submitters about project selection or about interviews to finalize selection.

Lists task deliverables: item 1 is a meeting agenda, minutes, and data management plan; item 3a is MoDOT providing the Offeror with examples of legal land descriptions; item 3c is a demonstration of AI writing a legal land description; item 4 is the Offeror providing training to ROW staff on how to use the tool; item 5 is a draft report, summary, and user manual; item 6 is a final report, summary, presentation, and user manual.

Project schedule is an estimate presuming the project starts November 1, 2024; proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline; alternative timelines will be considered but an extension is unlikely; the timeline will be finalized during the contracting phase. Quarterly updates on work accomplished are due on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December during the project, submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager, and are the basis for information in the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report that the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA at the end of each quarter of the fiscal year. An interim presentation must be scheduled near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and direction and to evaluate progress and determine if mid-project corrections are necessary, in addition to ongoing communication between the Principal Investigator(s) and MoDOT contacts. Monthly e-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts are required to provide ongoing updates of progress.

The chunk sets the project schedule and communication requirements for the MoDOT project: monthly e-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts are required to provide ongoing progress updates. Milestones: 11/15/2024 kick-off meeting with MoDOT to discuss project requirements and deliverables, with key milestone and deliverable dates determined from that meeting; 12/4/2024 data management plan due; 12/20/2024 MoDOT provides examples of approved legal land descriptions to the Offeror; 4/25/2025 Offeror presents how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs and MoDOT provides feedback; 7/25/2025 after tool adjustments, Offeror creates a manual and provides training to ROW staff; 9/15/2025 interim presentation must be done; 11/3/2025 draft final report, summary report and user manual due (submitted approximately two months prior to the final report); 1/1/2026 final report, summary report, presentation and user manual due (approximately one month before contract end, to allow billing to be completed); 2/2/2026 final invoice due and contract ends.

The successful Offeror shall provide the services described in (B), with a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000. Task descriptions are intended to provide guidance in development of the research. MoDOT is seeking the input of proposers to determine the best strategies to accomplish the research objectives.

Under "(B) Specific Requirements" of Section (2) Scope of Work, the Offeror must provide Construction and Materials with an electronic copy of a program proposal. The proposal is intended to help bring the project to its successful completion. No further detail on content, dates, or evaluation is given in this chunk.

Task 1 (Project Management) requires the Offeror to facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule, and to establish a protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination with the team. The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings reviewing progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next period; meetings may be in-person or online. The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and each quarterly status meeting. The finalized work plan will detail implementation of the following tasks plus the resources and schedule required. The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan (DMP) to MoDOT within 2 weeks after the project kick-off meeting, describing anticipated format(s) of data and related files and how platform-independent and non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.

Task 2 of the specific requirements is a Literature Review. It requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for ROW (right-of-way) purposes to be conducted.
Task 3a: MoDOT will provide copies of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions (LLDs) to the Offeror. The purpose is to help train the machine.

Before work begins on the proof of concepts, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the LLDs. MoDOT Information Systems must give approval before moving forward with Task 3c. This is part of Task 3b: Offeror Provides Program to Develop LLDs.

Task 3c is a proof of concept that AI/ML can develop legal land descriptions. The Offeror must demonstrate how the technology will create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties. MoDOT will review the drafts and provide feedback on how they can be improved.

Task 4 is "Training and User Manual". Once the system has been developed and finalized, the Offeror will provide training to ROW staff. The training will also include a user manual for staff to reference.

Task 5 requires the Offeror to prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary plus all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study. The drafts should be final products except for revisions based on MoDOT's review. A final report must include a completed Technical Report Documentation page. The chunk refers to the Publication Guidelines and summary template on the website.

Task 6 requires the Offeror to develop a final report detailing the tasks completed during the project, including any and all findings generated during the project's duration. The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions. A presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing important or significant details of the project must be provided. The chunk refers Offerors to the Publications Guidelines for the report and research summary, which can be found on the website.

The Offeror must consult MHTC's representative about any concerns involved with the administration of the services provided under this RFP. This falls under "(C) Administration of Program" in Section (2): Scope of Work.

Proposals must be emailed by 10 a.m. Central according to the time stamp on the due date indicated. Any form containing a signature line in this RFP, plus any amendments and pricing pages, may be electronically signed or manually signed, scanned and returned as part of the proposal. Proposals must reference the project number and title because more than one RFP may be due at one time. Proposals are to be emailed to the Research Director at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov.

The Offeror must respond to this RFP by submitting all data required in paragraph (B) for its proposal to be evaluated and considered for award. Failure to submit such data is deemed sufficient cause for disqualification of a proposal from further consideration.

All questions regarding specifications, requirements, the competitive procurement process, or other questions must be directed to the Research Director at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov. Questions must be submitted by the date and time listed in section 1E.

The chunk identifies the "Proposal Submission Form" as a required element of the proposal under Section (3) "Proposal Submission Information", subsection (B) "Required Elements of Proposal", item (1). It states the form can be found at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers. No other details, dates, amounts or criteria are given.

The proposal must include a narrative-style Work Plan describing how the Offeror will work with MoDOT to fulfill project-specific requirements. The Work Plan section is limited to ten (10) pages with font size no less than 12 points; the limit excludes forms or resumes attached to the proposal. The project plan shall include all items outlined in Section 2 and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans.

The Personnel section of the required proposal elements asks the Offeror to indicate the name, location, telephone number, and email address of the primary contact person. Information in this section should highlight previous Offeror experience and any relevant work with other state agencies or local governments in Missouri. The Offeror must furnish a complete listing of each Sub-Offeror, if any, with complete contact information for that Sub-Offeror.

Proposals must clearly identify experience in offering the services requested in this RFP during the past three (3) years. The experience description should include a list of the agencies the institution has served or currently serves. This is element (4) Experience under (B) Required Elements of Proposal in Section (3) Proposal Submission Information.

Proposals should indicate the name, title, and telephone number of at least three officials of clients within the past three years (References). Proposals must be submitted as one combined PDF document. The submission should only include the required documents organized in this order: 1) Proposal Submission Form; 2) Cover Letter (Optional; 1 page maximum); 3) Body of Proposal (including work plan and project schedule); 4) Personnel; 5) Organization's Project Experience; 6) Team Member Experience; and 7) Organization's Client References.

Any agreement for services resulting from this RFP shall be awarded to the Offeror providing the best proposal. After determining responsiveness, proposals will be evaluated in accordance with criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee. The chunk does not list the specific criteria or weights.

The Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate for all services defined in the Scope of Work. The estimate must be shown on Section (4), Price Page, of the proposal, which must be completed, signed, and returned with the Offeror's proposal. A detailed budget will be developed at a later date. A template is referenced at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.

The chunk is the Cost Estimate price page (Section 4(A)) of the RFP. Offerors must indicate all costs for providing services in accordance with the provisions and requirements stated in the RFP. The cost estimate table has line items for Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous (list - attach additional sheet if needed), and Total, each with an "Estimated Amount" column.

The RFP is governed by the contract provisions listed in this section, and award is subject to a post-award negotiated contract. The same contract provisions will appear in the post-award negotiated contract. If the parties cannot agree to terms in the post-award contract, MHTC reserves the right to cancel the award of the RFP and contract and select a different Offeror.

MoDOT's Research Director, Jen Harper, is designated as MHTC's representative for administering the Agreement's provisions as defined in Paragraph (E) of this section. MHTC's representative may designate other persons with authority to act on behalf of MHTC in furtherance of the Agreement's performance. The Offeror shall fully coordinate its activities for MHTC with those of the Construction and Materials Division. The Offeror shall make advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to the Construction and Materials Division throughout the effective period.

Offerors are encouraged to submit copies of their existing affirmative action programs, if any, and to directly hire minorities and women as direct employees. Offerors are encouraged to obtain minority business enterprise (MBE) and women business enterprise (WBE) participation in this work through subcontractors, suppliers, joint ventures, or other arrangements, with a target of 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation. Regardless of any subcontractors or suppliers used, the Offeror remains responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality/performance of the services.

Chunk is section (K) "Non-employment of Unauthorized Aliens" of the agreement requirements. It cites Section 285.530, RSMo., prohibiting business entities or employers from knowingly employing, hiring for employment, or continuing to employ an unauthorized alien to perform work within the State of Missouri. As a condition for award of any contract or grant in excess of five thousand dollars ($5,000) by the State or a political subdivision, or for any business entity receiving a state-administered or subsidized tax credit, tax abatement, or loan from the state, the business entity must: (1) by sworn affidavit and documentation, affirm enrollment and participation in a federal work authorization program (E-Verify given as an example) for employees working in connection with the contracted services, providing a completed copy of the E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) as acceptable documentation, with E-Verify available at https://www.e-verify.gov/ for entities not already enrolled; and (2) by sworn affidavit, affirm it does not knowingly employ any unauthorized alien in connection with the contracted services. The affidavit is provided in this document as Exhibit A.

Chunk is Section (5) "(L) Proof of Lawful Presence for Sole Proprietorships and Partnerships" of the RFP. If the business entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership, pursuant to Section 208.009, RSMo., each sole proprietor and each general partner must provide affirmative proof of lawful presence in the United States. Such entity is eligible for temporary public benefits upon submission by each sole proprietor and general partner of a sworn affidavit of lawful presence until lawful presence is affirmatively determined, or as otherwise provided by Section 208.009, RSMo. A copy of the affidavit is provided within the document as Exhibit B.

- Clause (Q) "Ownership of Reports" in Section (5) "Agreement Requirements" states that all documents, reports, exhibits, etc. produced by the Offeror at the direction of MHTC's representative remain the property of MHTC.
- Information supplied by MHTC's representative also remains the property of MHTC.
- The client/issuing body is referred to as MHTC.

The Offeror must maintain all working papers and records relating to the Agreement. Records must be made available at all reasonable times at no charge to MHTC and/or the Missouri State Auditor during the term of the Agreement and any extension, and for three (3) years from the date of final payment under the Agreement. MHTC's representative has the right to reproduce and/or use any products derived from the Offeror's work without payment of royalties, fees, etc. MHTC's representative has the right at all times to audit any and all records pertaining to the services.

Prior to contract signing, the Offeror may be asked about its ability to provide certificates of insurance meeting, or approaching, specified coverages. General Liability: not less than $500,000 for any one person in a single accident or occurrence, and not less than $3,000,000 for all claims arising out of a single occurrence. Automobile Liability: not less than $500,000 for any one person in a single accident or occurrence, and not less than $3,000,000 for all claims arising out of a single occurrence. A Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent in accordance with state law is required.

The client is MoDOT (Missouri Department of Transportation), referenced in the licensing-approval requirement. All applications must be developed using approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or .NET Framework (currently supported .NET 6.0 or above unless a specific need exists; if .NET Framework is required, a currently supported 4.8 release or above, per the .NET and .NET Core official support policy on microsoft.com). Web applications must use the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework, and library dependencies should be reviewed/updated annually. Approved programming languages are C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python; Python is reserved for ESRI scripts and other small one-time uses, with large-scale use requiring approval of the Information Systems (IS) Best Practices Review Team (BRPT), and version 3.x from www.python.org should be used for other platforms. Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management; all customer applications should be web-based browser applications tested and designed for the latest IS-approved browser(s) at a minimum.

Technical constraints for applications: must be tested and designed to use the latest IS approved browser(s) at a minimum; no client-side software other than a modern browser may be required (no Java Applets, no Silverlight). On-premise database deployments must run on Oracle 19C, or be designed and maintained to run on the latest supported version of SQL Server, with Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher allowed in certain cases if approved by the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team. No Personal Identifiable Information (PII) may be stored in any database table unless the application has a specific business need; all stored PII must have approval from the IS Cyber Security Team. All web applications must meet the State of Missouri's Accessibility Standard, based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (as amended) and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (see Accessibility (mo.gov)), and must adhere to W3 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance (WCAG 2.1 AA). Copyright/attribution rules: never use text, diagrams, photographs, audio, multimedia, program source code, script or graphics from another author's web pages unless the author explicitly permits free copying or appropriate arrangements are made; vendor logos, branding or company endorsements must not appear if there is a supported, licensed way to eliminate them.
